name: IFEval
summary: 541 instruction-following prompts with automatically checkable requirements for format, length, language, keywords, and other response constraints.
overview:
IFEval (Instruction-Following Eval) measures how well language models obey explicit response constraints. The original benchmark introduced 25 instruction types, including length limits, required or forbidden words, capitalization, output format, and response language. It was introduced in November 2023. [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.07911)

Each prompt asks for a free-form response that can satisfy one or several verifiable requirements. The checks focus on these requirements; they do not require one canonical response. [Instruction registry](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/blob/e6890f85757dd84e27ca6df2dd30651dafad28e0/instruction_following_eval/instructions_registry.py) and [checker implementations](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/blob/e6890f85757dd84e27ca6df2dd30651dafad28e0/instruction_following_eval/instructions.py)
methodology:
This snapshot includes all 541 records in instruction_following_eval/data/input_data.jsonl at the pinned Google Research commit. This is the original IFEval prompt set; the authors’ Hugging Face mirror labels the same evaluation data as a train split. The snapshot has 541 distinct prompts and IDs, with 305 single-instruction, 179 two-instruction, and 57 three-instruction tasks. These counts are calculated from the pinned source. [Original records](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/blob/e6890f85757dd84e27ca6df2dd30651dafad28e0/instruction_following_eval/data/input_data.jsonl) and [authors’ dataset card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/IFEval)

Task Prompts preserve each upstream prompt verbatim, including line breaks and trailing whitespace. IDs are the original integer key values represented as decimal strings. Each Source link opens the exact immutable JSONL line, including its ordered instruction_id_list and matching kwargs grading parameters. These evaluator parameters are not added to the model’s prompt.

The dataset supplies no canonical reference answers. No solution text or example model responses are imported. Each task’s Environment link opens the official evaluator setup instructions; its grading functions resolve the task’s instruction IDs through the registry. Reading the prompts requires no special environment. [Evaluator setup](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/blob/e6890f85757dd84e27ca6df2dd30651dafad28e0/instruction_following_eval/README.md#how-to-run), [grading functions](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/blob/e6890f85757dd84e27ca6df2dd30651dafad28e0/instruction_following_eval/evaluation_lib.py), and [instruction registry](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/blob/e6890f85757dd84e27ca6df2dd30651dafad28e0/instruction_following_eval/instructions_registry.py)

The importer uses only Python’s standard library, honors dataset_revision, and checks the downloaded source’s SHA-256 before replacing the snapshot. Run python3 data/ifeval/import.py to reproduce the import.
scoring:
The official evaluator reports four accuracy measures: prompt-level strict, instruction-level strict, prompt-level loose, and instruction-level loose. Prompt-level accuracy is the fraction of prompts whose listed instructions all pass; instruction-level accuracy is the fraction of all listed instructions that pass. Empty responses fail. [Evaluation and aggregation](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/blob/e6890f85757dd84e27ca6df2dd30651dafad28e0/instruction_following_eval/evaluation_lib.py)

Strict evaluation checks the original response. Loose evaluation accepts an instruction if any of eight response variants passes: the original text, text with asterisks removed, text without its first line, last line, or both, and combinations of those line removals with asterisk removal. Each instruction may pass on a different variant. [Loose evaluation](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/blob/e6890f85757dd84e27ca6df2dd30651dafad28e0/instruction_following_eval/evaluation_lib.py#L98-L146)

Compare scores using the same metric, source revision, prompting, and response-generation settings. Benchopedia's sweep uses the official strict prompt-level rule. One attempt passes when the response follows every listed instruction.
limitations:
IFEval covers a finite set of mechanically checkable instructions. It does not comprehensively evaluate subjective requirements such as tone, overall writing quality, or factual correctness. The authors identify limited instruction diversity and real-world coverage as areas for improvement. Strict checks can reject reasonable formatting variations; loose checks can accept responses that fail the original requirement. [Discussion and metric caveats](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.07911)

The exact checks depend on the pinned implementation, including its text processing and language detection. A high score establishes success on those checks, not fulfillment of every aspect of the underlying request. [Checker implementations](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/blob/e6890f85757dd84e27ca6df2dd30651dafad28e0/instruction_following_eval/instructions.py)

Some prompts refer to external webpages. Those pages are not included in this snapshot and can change or become unavailable. The original prompts and evaluator parameters are preserved as published, without independent correction. [Prompt source](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/blob/e6890f85757dd84e27ca6df2dd30651dafad28e0/instruction_following_eval/data/input_data.jsonl)
